core_obligations: The sieve family is a topology (proof lines 11479-11499): the axioms of a site directly imply the axioms of a topology, and the author writes out the verification of one of them, the stability under base change, by refining the covering twice and using the transitivity axiom for sites.

From the topology to the site (proof lines 11501-11547): a presheaf satisfying the sheaf condition for the topology is shown to satisfy the sheaf condition for coverings of the site, by passing to the sieve generated by the covering, using that this sieve belongs to the defined topology, and constructing the amalgamating section as a morphism on the sieve using the given compatible family.
The converse direction is the evident one and completes the equivalence of sheaf conditions.
proof_roadmap: Match the axioms of a site with the axioms of a topology, writing out the base change axiom.
Show that a sheaf for the topology satisfies the sheaf condition for coverings of the site.
Record the converse, which is immediate from the definition of the topology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares the two ways of presenting a site: it shows that the sieves refining coverings form a topology, and that the sheaves for this topology are exactly the sheaves on the given site (statement lines 11460-11476). The proof is a complete argument: the first assertion is obtained by matching the axioms of a site with the axioms of a topology, with the base change axiom verified in detail by two successive refinements (proof lines 11479-11499); the second is proved by passing from a covering of the site to the sieve it generates, using that this sieve belongs to the topology, and constructing the amalgamating section as a morphism on that sieve from the given compatible family (proof lines 11501-11547). The non-formal content is the two verifications, both written out. The claim is H2: a structured verification with the axioms named.
